hints.title: Interval Overlap
hints.text: Each falling square occupies an open horizontal interval from left to left plus side length. It lands on any previous square whose interval overlaps.

hints.title: Base Height Determination
hints.text: Two intervals [l1, r1] and [l2, r2] overlap if and only if l1 is strictly less than r2 and l2 is strictly less than r1.

hints.title: Interval Simulation
hints.text: For each square, inspect all previously placed squares that overlap horizontally. The new height is the maximum top height among overlapping squares plus the square side length. Track the running maximum height.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def fallingSquares(self, positions: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        intervals = []
        ans = []
        max_h = 0

        for left, size in positions:
            right = left + size
            base_h = 0
            for prev_l, prev_r, prev_h in intervals:
                if left < prev_r and right > prev_l:
                    base_h = max(base_h, prev_h)
            cur_h = base_h + size
            intervals.append((left, right, cur_h))
            max_h = max(max_h, cur_h)
            ans.append(max_h)

        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Quadratic interval intersection check tracking running maximum heights.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Discrete grid simulation over large coordinate ranges (up to 10^8) exceeds memory limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing intervals explicitly requires only O(N) space and runs within 1000 operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use open interval conditions left < prev_r and right > prev_l to avoid edge touch collisions.
